subject: Proposal: Renewal term + Priority Support migration for Nimbus Labs
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbuslabs.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbuslabs.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — capacity growth + priority support

Hi Irene,

Hope you're well. We're coming up on the end of our first contract year on 2026-09-30 and wanted to start the conversation about renewal. A few things that matter to us: 

- We expect platform usage to ~2x over the next 12 months (primarily text-generation throughput and embeddings).
- We're interested in upgrading to Priority (premium) Support with a 24/7 on-call rota and a 99.9% latency SLO on inference paths for our production model.
- We'd like clearer terms around burst capacity and a predictable pricing model for committed throughput.

Can you send initial options for term lengths (12 vs 24 months), committed throughput tiers, and an estimated uplift on pricing for the premium support add-on? Also attaching our usage export for July which shows the current baseline.

Attachment: nimbus-usage-2026-07.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Labs
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity growth + priority support

Marissa, Ben — forwarding Nimbus's note and usage file. They want to: 1) double committed capacity, 2) add Priority Support (24/7 oncall + latency SLO), and 3) clarity on burst behavior and pricing.

Notes / asks:
- Marissa: can Ops validate a realistic ramp plan to 2x and confirm how long we need to fully provision reserved GPUs vs burst pool? Please include runbook changes and onboarding time for oncall.
- Ben: can you draft two commercial options (12m / 24m) with committed throughput bands and the premium support add-on as a priced SKU? Consider offering a one-time migration credit or first-month usage credit to ease the bump.

I think we should propose a 60–90 day phased ramp with a defined burst policy (e.g., 2x baseline burst for 30 days, then cap unless committed). For the latency SLO wording, we can offer SLO targets on inference paths at 99.9% p95 under committed throughput and an operational clause for allowed maintenance windows. I'll let Marissa define achievable SLO/ops commitments.

Quoted message below.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbuslabs.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity growth + priority support

Hi Samantha — thanks for the details and the usage file. Quick outline for proposal (high level):

Option A — 12 months
- Committed throughput band: 2x current baseline (guaranteed capacity)
- Premium Support add-on: 24/7 oncall, 60-minute P1 response, 99.9% p95 latency SLO on committed paths
- Price uplift: +28% on committed token/throughput rate; Premium Support fee: $25,000/month
- Burst policy: 2x baseline for first 30 days post-renewal; bursts billed at overage rate thereafter unless converted to committed capacity

Option B — 24 months (preferred for pricing)
- Same committed band as above but with a 15% uplift instead of 28% and Premium Support fee: $18,000/month (discounted)
- Includes one-time migration credit equal to 10% of first month committed spend

I've attached a draft SLA/terms doc for your review — it calls out SLO definitions, measurement windows, maintenance windows, and credits/penalties. If these look reasonable, we can schedule a short call next week to agree on the preferred term and route to procurement / DocuSign.

Attachment: nimbus-draft-sla-terms_v1.docx (DOCX, 92KB)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbuslabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbuslabs.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity growth + priority support

Hi Ben / Irene — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. Nimbus is comfortable moving forward on Option B (24 months) provided final SLA wording is aligned with the 99.9% latency target and that the migration credit is applied on the first invoice. Procurement is copied; please route the final document for signature and include the DocuSign link and payment instructions.

Next steps we expect:
- Redwood to send final SLA + contract with the 24m term and applied migration credit.
- DocuSign circulation to Procurement (procurement@nimbuslabs.com).
- Kickoff for ops/oncall onboarding two weeks after signature.

DocuSign routing preferred. Thanks — looking forward to closing.

— Samantha
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Labs
